fsGroup.description: A special supplemental group that applies to all containers in a pod. Some volume types allow the Kubelet to change the ownership of that volume to be owned by the pod: 1. The owning GID will be the FSGroup 2. The setgid bit is set (new files created in the volume will be owned by FSGroup) 3. The permission bits are OR'd with rw-rw----. If unset, the Kubelet will not modify the ownership and permissions of any volume.

fsGroupChangePolicy.description: fsGroupChangePolicy defines behavior of changing ownership and permission of the volume before being exposed inside Pod. If true, the Kubelet will validate the image at runtime to ensure that it does not run as UID 0 (root) and fail to start the container if it does. certManager.description:
Manage the TLS certificate through cert-manager instead of supplying it directly
For nginx/contour, the chart creates a cert-manager `Certificate` issuing into
`secretName`. For OpenShift Routes, the chart instead adds cert-manager.io/*
annotations and relies on the openshift-routes controller
(github.com/cert-manager/openshift-routes) being installed to patch the Route.
IMPORTANT: For OpenShift Routes, you MUST have cert-manager/openshift-routes
installed in your cluster. It is NOT included with the standard cert-manager
or Red Hat's cert-manager Operator. Install it with:
`helm install openshift-routes -n cert-manager oci://ghcr.io/cert-manager/charts/openshift-routes`
Routes without the openshift-routes controller will have annotations but no
certificate will be populated into spec.tls.

chart does not render; "passthrough" hands the connection to the pod untouched and is
incompatible with the path-based routing the chart emits.

scc.description: OpenShift SecurityContextConstraints. Ignored on every other platform.

binding.description:
How the SCC is granted to this release's ServiceAccounts.
cluster   - ClusterRoleBinding. Cluster-scoped, needs cluster administrator rights.
namespace - RoleBinding in the release namespace. Keeps the grant local; use when
            the cluster forbids ClusterRoleBindings for application workloads.
none      - The chart grants nothing; an administrator binds the SCC out of band.
Empty (default) follows `platform`: cluster on openshift, none elsewhere.
Empty rather than null because helm-schema drops null from a generated enum,
which would make the default fail validation against this chart's own schema.
binding.title: binding

create.description:
Create the SecurityContextConstraints and its backing ClusterRole.
Both are CLUSTER-SCOPED, so this requires cluster administrator privileges.
null (default) follows `platform`: true on openshift, false elsewhere.
Set to false when an administrator applies them out of band, and pair it with
`binding: namespace` so the release still grants itself the SCC from inside its
own namespace. See examples/openshift/scc-namespace-scoped.yaml.
create.title: create

name.description:
Name of the SecurityContextConstraints to create and/or grant.
Empty uses "<fullname>-scc". Override to point the binding at an SCC that an
administrator applied under a different name.
name.title: name
